# DropSpace 1.1 Beta4

<!-- update-summary: Adds a liquid-glass background to the existing Dynamic Island, with adjustable blur, refraction, dispersion, dark overlay and black-to-glass gradient while preserving its content, layout and controls. -->

## Changes

- The existing island gains an independently implemented GPU liquid-glass material. Background blur, edge refraction, RGB dispersion and a black-to-glass gradient affect only the material behind the original content.
- Settings include island style, background blur (0–30), refraction (0–400%), dispersion (0–100), dark overlay (0–200%) and the gradient switch, in all ten UI languages.
- The requested defaults are liquid glass, blur **1**, refraction **400%**, dispersion **75**, dark overlay **0%**, and the gradient **on**. Existing profiles without these fields receive those defaults; their other preferences are preserved.
- Desktop Acrylic remains selectable. Unavailable capture or graphics support falls back to the previous material. High contrast, reduced effects, disabled transparency and remote sessions retain their existing accessible fallback behavior.

The island's content, geometry, typography, toolbar, controls, hit targets and interactions are unchanged. The live glass material uses in-memory desktop sampling and excludes the island from screenshots and recordings to prevent self-feedback. No screen image is stored or transmitted by this material.

v1.1.0-beta.3 is the immediate upgrade baseline for this release. Existing settings, content, lyrics matching, source preferences, model files and independent CUDA component bytes are preserved.

## Local test build

Windows x64 build 20348 or later. The local installer and portable executable are test artifacts; no public release or updater promotion is implied. See the [validation record](../../docs/dev/1.1-beta4-liquid-glass.md) for actual checks and limits.

The pre-existing native heap crash (`0xc0000374`) has not been proven fixed. This update does not claim long-term native stability, or validation across every GPU, monitor/DPI combination or remote-session configuration.
